mainEntity.name: How do spray foam and fiberglass batts compare for moisture management?

acceptedAnswer.text: Closed-cell spray foam acts as both an insulation layer and a built-in vapor retarder, while fiberglass batts require a separate, carefully detailed vapor and air barrier. Closed-cell foam creates a rigid, airtight seal that blocks bulk water and vapor movement, which is beneficial in crawlspaces and exterior envelopes. Fiberglass offers a lower upfront installation cost and easy adjustment around utilities, but it remains vapor-permeable and relies entirely on external house wraps or interior membranes to manage humidity.
